summary.value: Table component, used to display tabular data. Renders a native HTML table element.

a11y.method: drafted from the docs page, quote-verified, NOT yet human-reviewed

value.rule: Table cells must not be merged, and each cell should contain only one interactive element
value.quote: Table cells should not be merged, and each cell should contain only one interactive element.

value.rule: Use row and/or column headers so screen reader users can navigate the table
value.quote: For screen reader users to navigate the content, it is important to use row and/or column headers ( <Table.HeaderCell> ).

value.rule: Mark headers with scope="row" or scope="col" to indicate what they apply to
value.quote: Use scope="row" and scope="col" to indicate whether the header applies to a row or a column.

value.rule: Headers may be visually hidden if space is limited
value.quote: If space is limited, you may visually hide one or more headers.

value.rule: Tables must always include a caption describing what the table shows, since screen readers read it first
value.quote: Tables must always include a caption element that provides a brief description of what the table shows. Screen readers will read the caption, allowing users to decide whether they want to continue reading the table.

value.rule: Empty cells must use Table.Cell so screen readers can navigate the table correctly
value.quote: Empty cells must use Table.Cell . This is important to ensure that screen readers can navigate the table correctly.

value.rule: Make sure sorting can be changed using the keyboard
value.quote: Make sure you can change the sorting using the keyboard.

value.rule: Test sorting with a screen reader to confirm sortable state, sort direction, and that focus isn't lost when sorting changes
value.quote: Test with a screen reader to verify that you hear what is sortable, the sorting types, and that focus is not lost when sorting changes.

value.rule: Tables are challenging on mobile; common adaptations are horizontal scroll or converting to a list view
value.quote: Tables can be challenging on mobile, as there is no universal design that works well in all contexts. The most common approaches are a table that scrolls horizontally or converting the table into a list view.

relations.method: drafted from the docs page, quote-verified, NOT yet human-reviewed

value.note: Prefer a list view over a table when the content is better suited to a list
value.quote: the information is better suited to a list or card view

value.note: Prefer a card view over a table when the content is better suited to cards
value.quote: the information is better suited to a list or card view

composition.method: drafted from the docs page, quote-verified, NOT yet human-reviewed

value.rule: Use table to compare information, present clearly structured row/column data, or support sorting
value.quote: Use table when the goal is to help users compare information easily the data needs a clear structure with rows and columns the content can benefit from sorting

value.rule: Avoid table for page layout, when content is very limited without need for comparison, or when large data sets become hard to read on mobile
value.quote: Avoid using table when the purpose is to create layout or visually organise content on a page the information is better suited to a list or card view the content is very limited, for example only one column or very few data points without a need for comparison the table becomes difficult to read on mobile because the data set is large

value.rule: Use table to structure and present data clearly in rows and columns
value.quote: Use table to structure and present data clearly in rows and columns.

value.rule: Content should be left-aligned except numbers, which should be right-aligned for easier comparison
value.quote: Content in tables should be left-aligned, except for numbers, which should be right-aligned to make comparison easier.

value.rule: Use Table.HeaderCell (not Table.Cell) for cells that describe the content of their row or column
value.quote: Use <Table.HeaderCell> for header cells, not <Table.Cell> . A cell counts as a header when it describes the content of the same row or column.

value.rule: In rows with several actions, a menu can be used to save space when the actions don't need to be visible at all times
value.quote: In table rows with several actions, you can use a menu to save space if the actions do not need to be visible at all times.

value.rule: When numbers are meant to be compared, align them to the right within the cell
value.quote: When numbers appear in a table and are meant to be compared, align them to the right within the cell.

value.rule: Avoid long texts in table cells; keep content short and concise so it's easy to scan across rows and columns
value.quote: Avoid long texts in table cells. Keep content short and concise so it is easy to scan across rows and columns.

value.rule: If more information is needed than fits in a cell, consider linking to a detail page
value.quote: If you need to show more information, consider linking to a detail page.

value.rule: Use headers to tell users what type of content they'll find in rows and columns
value.quote: Use headers to tell users what type of content they will find in the rows and columns.

value.rule: Content in cells should generally be left-aligned; exceptions are numbers, currency, and sometimes form elements and buttons
value.quote: As a general rule, content in cells should be left-aligned to make it easier to read and scan. The exception is numbers and currency and sometimes form elements and buttons.
